_comment: OPS-DEPLOY-INTERLOCK-CRON-DEFER-W1, made PER-HOST by OPS-HOST-AUTO-REBOOT-W1 — the DECLARED set of scheduled work a HOST-LEVEL DISRUPTION can decapitate. Read by ops/scripts/deploy-cron-interlock.sh (signal-1 deploys) and ops/monitoring/kernel-auto-reboot.sh (aoe-1 and, since OPS-HOST-AUTO-REBOOT-SIGNAL1-PROMOTE-W1, signal-1 reboots — the `reboot` event; see `_disruption_events`), asserted by scripts/check-cron-interlock-coverage.mjs. THE CLASSIFICATION IS THE DELIVERABLE; the dispatch code around it is small. EVERY ROW DECLARES ITS `host`, and `_enumeration` / `_containers` / `_residual_no_safe_kill` are keyed by host — because the DISRUPTION EVENT differs per host and so does the enumeration that finds it. signal-1's event is `docker compose up --force-recreate`, which kills `docker exec`s; aoe-1's is a REBOOT, which is strictly larger — it stops every container, every host process and every in-flight Prefect run, so a `docker exec` grep is the WRONG INSTRUMENT there and would have produced a 1-row population and a structurally vacuous gate on the only host that reboots. Placement is DERIVED, not taste: check-declaration-coverage.mjs pins CONSUMER_DIRS = ['ops/monitoring','ops/cron'], so a declaration read only from ops/scripts/ has zero readers there and would sit half-declared; and it needs no sync because deploy.yml runs `git reset --hard origin/main` BEFORE it invokes the interlock, so this file is always current at the only moment it is ever read. (monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py's ORPHAN scan is scoped to MONITORING_DIR=/opt/algovault-monitoring and never sees ops/scripts/ — the CONSUMER_DIRS leg is the load-bearing one.)

_classes.safe-to-kill: Atomic-replace publish, checkpoint-resumable, or idempotent on next fire. The deploy does NOTHING. The row exists so a future reader sees the job was CONSIDERED, not missed.
_classes.preempt-and-catchup: Killing loses work that a bounded catch-up can repair. SIGTERM, wait up to the derived budget for a checkpoint, then launch an SLO-gated catch-up detached.
_classes.no-safe-kill: Neither atomic nor repairable. Bounded wait, then PROCEED ANYWAY with a loud DEFERRED record. A deploy must never hang on a batch job.
_classes._indeterminate: A row whose `reason` is missing or empty is INDETERMINATE, never a silent safe-to-kill. Same convention as schedule-boundary-rule.json's exemptions.

deploy.note: Rows are keyed by PROCESS PATTERN, not by cron line: the interlock matches patterns, and one pattern (seed-signals.js) covers 28 cron lines. `cron_lines` on each row records the fan-out so the enumeration stays recoverable. The prior enumeration measured 91 active lines (OPS-HOST-KERNEL-REBOOT-W2) and 75 before that (W1) — re-derive, never inherit. Re-derived 2026-08-31T13:43Z by OPS-BAND-OUTCOME-WIRE-W1: 100 -> 106 active lines in two days, `docker exec` lines unchanged at 46. The growth is entirely in host-process lines, so no row's classification moves; the count is corrected because a stale enumeration makes every interlock decision built on it wrong, and this file's own instruction is to re-derive rather than inherit. || Re-derived 2026-09-08T07:47Z by IDENTITY-LIFECYCLE-W3 CH1: 106 -> 118 active lines. reboot.command: crontab -l   # every active line   &&   systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend --plain | awk '{print $1}'   &&   systemctl list-unit-files --type=timer --state=enabled --no-legend | awk '{print $1}'   — the UNION is the population, because a reboot stops all of it. This is exactly what kernel-auto-reboot.sh feeds check-cron-interlock-coverage.mjs --event reboot on every run, so the enumeration is re-derived live each hour rather than inherited from this block.
reboot.note: A REBOOT kills every container AND every host process, so every live line/unit maps to a row or exclusion by explicit cron_match / units — none by inference. Measured 2026-10-02 (crontab sha256 93f9e3ef…): 126 active lines (125 before this wave's own `16 * * * *` harness line), 22 running services, 28 enabled timers. Transient run-*.service units are deliberately left unmapped: an operator one-shot in flight DEFERS the reboot until it ends.

rows.reason: It sends an on-chain Base-mainnet `publishRoot` transaction and THEN writes the batch row + per-signal proofs to Postgres. Measured 2026-08-29: tx confirmed 00:05:04.169Z, batch complete 00:05:07.639Z — a ~3.5s window in which a recreate leaves a Merkle root committed on chain with no database record of it. Re-running does not repair that: getNextBatchId() mints a NEW batch id, so the orphaned root is permanent. Not atomic, not resumable, not idempotent — the only row in this registry that is genuinely none of the three.

The whole job is ~7s, so a 120s bounded wait covers it comfortably — the deploy is delayed by at most one job length and then PROCEEDS regardless.

rows.reason: A 7h+ weekly LLM probe sweep with no checkpoint and no resume: a kill loses the whole week's GEO measurement, the next fire is 7 days away, and re-running costs real LLM spend for data that is dated to its run week. rows.notes: THE ONLY THING THAT EVER FLIPS A STEP TO LIVE. No human does, by design (architect ruling Q1(A)). rows.notes: Same engine, same suppression, same caps as the four usage steps — a fifth step, not a second mailer. Deliberately NOT registered in the 15-minute dispatcher: its cadence is the RELEASE cadence, and registering it there would evaluate a 'what's new' 96 times a day for a message that can be sent once a month. Body is the README `## What's new in vX.Y.0` block converted VERBATIM; recap sub-sections are excluded because they are a rolling 3-minor window and would re-send content a reader already had. Blocks BATCH into one email so two releases in a month is still one message. Verdict token LIFECYCLE_DIGEST_VERDICT= maps PASS=0/FAIL=1/INDETERMINATE=3. Zero opt-ins and zero blocks are both reported as explicit PASS facts, never as a silent success.

rows.reason: THE PACKAGE MANAGER INSTALLS THE KERNEL THIS HARNESS EXISTS TO LOAD. An interrupted dpkg leaves /var/lib/dpkg/updates dirty (u-u self-heals with `dpkg --configure -a` next run), but a kill during the kernel's initramfs/grub trigger can leave a broken initrd behind the default boot entry, and nothing repairs that before the next boot. unattended-upgrade-shutdown holds a logind delay inhibitor (InhibitDelayMaxSec=30) and lets the in-flight dpkg step finish, but that path has never been exercised on either host (its log is 0 bytes) — so the harness never reboots while it runs. The pattern is the SERVICE argv, not `unattended-upgrade` (that always matches the resident shutdown handler) and not `/usr/bin/dpkg` (the auto-fix path runs a PATH dpkg).

exclusions.what: The 42 active cron lines on signal-1 that never reach a crypto-quant-signal-mcp-* container. 100 active lines, 46 with a direct `docker exec`, 12 more reaching one through a host script — 58 covered by `rows`, 42 excluded here.
exclusions.reason: `docker compose up -d --build --force-recreate` recreates only the three services in /opt/crypto-quant-signal-mcp/docker-compose.yml. A cron that runs as a host process, or execs into a container belonging to another compose project, is not reachable by this deploy at all — there is nothing for an interlock to protect. Excluded by construction, not by judgement.
exclusions.re_derivation_command: crontab -l | grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)' | grep -v 'docker exec'   # then, for each resolved script path, `grep -E '(^|[;&|]|\$\(|\bexec[[:space:]])[[:space:]]*docker[[:space:]]+exec' <script>` and confirm it is empty

exclusions.reason: OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS DEPLOY, settled by probe rather than by assumption. It belongs to the algovault-bot repo (absent from this one), and it runs a HOST process — `/opt/algovault-bot/.venv/bin/python scripts/entitlement-drain.py` — with zero `docker exec` anywhere in it. `docker compose up --force-recreate` on the signal-mcp stack cannot touch it.
exclusions.separate_finding: Its SCHEDULE is a different problem and is deliberately NOT fixed here: those ten minutes occupy every canonical off-boundary slot in the hour, which is why signal-1 has only :09 and :39 free and why OPS-HOST-AUTO-REBOOT-W1 faces a 2-minute target. Filed as OPS-BOT-CRON-SCHEDULE-GREED-W1; it is a bot-repo change and cannot ship from a signal-mcp wave. Note also that the script's own header docstring claims `*/5 * * * *`, which the live crontab contradicts — the docstring is stale and belongs to the same follow-up.

exclusions.reason: Both contain the literal string `docker exec`, and neither invokes it. One occurrence is a `#` comment recording a RETIRED implementation; the other sits inside an alert-body heredoc ('... host dist/ unusable AND docker exec failed ...'). A mention is not an invocation — the same rule check-canaries-wired.mjs already carries for comments and check-test-budget.mjs carries for string literals. scripts/check-cron-interlock-coverage.mjs therefore matches `docker exec` only in COMMAND POSITION, after stripping comments.

deploy.ruling: The 18:00-02:59 UTC deploy-free window is NOT retired. It is now a DECLARED control with two named rows justifying it, both of which fire inside it (00:05 and Mon 01:00). What changes is that it stops being folklore carried by an agent-side memory file — a third rule source in an estate that declares two — and becomes data these rows own. OPS-HOST-AUTO-REBOOT-W1 should read this block, not the memory file.
deploy.retire_when: publish-merkle-batch writes its batch row in the same transaction boundary as (or before) its on-chain send, and geo-weekly-cron gains a checkpoint. Neither is in scope here.

reboot.ruling: Under a REBOOT these rows ABORT the run while in flight (retried next hour) — they never extend a window. Most finish in seconds (the bot drains <=10s, the alert engine p50 0.37s); the long ones are editorial-publish (<=3374s, 02:00Z timer) and geo-weekly-cron (Mon 01:00Z), both of which start before the 03:00Z window opens. The post-arm recheck closes the check-then-act gap for the every-minute bot alert engine.
reboot.retire_when: Each row's own repair: a claim-before-send (or send-then-claim with a dedupe key) for the Telegram senders, a checkpoint for geo-weekly-cron, a transaction boundary around publish-merkle-batch's on-chain send, an atomic write for snapshot-landing-daily. Not in scope here.

reboot.ruling: ZERO — and that is the measured reason aoe-1 is the right host to automate FIRST, not a gap in the enumeration. Every candidate is atomic-on-restart (8 containers, unless-stopped), idempotent on next fire (11 Prefect schedules, max 60.3s), or a read-only probe (7 crons, max 43s). Nothing on aoe-1 writes on-chain, publishes externally, or holds an unrepairable critical section — unlike signal-1, whose two no-safe-kill rows are exactly what keeps the 18:00-02:59 UTC deploy-free window alive.
reboot.gate_is_not_vacuous: kernel-auto-reboot.sh's third gate can therefore never ABORT today. That is a REPORTED pass, never a silent one: the gate prints the aoe-1 row count it evaluated, so a zero that means 'nothing is unsafe' stays distinguishable from a zero that means 'the filter is broken'. Its value is forward-looking — the day a no-safe-kill job lands on aoe-1, the reboot starts deferring without anyone remembering to wire it.

_hosts._why_per_host: A row consulted for the wrong host is a guard reading a green light for a road it is not on. Every consumer MUST filter rows by the host it is acting on, resolved through the estate's identity chain (MONITORING_HOST_LABELS -> /etc/algovault-host-label -> REFUSE), never a default.

_disruption_events._semantics: Which disruption events each host has. Every row declares `events[]` (never a default) and every consumer filters by (host, event): deploy-cron-interlock.sh reads `deploy`, kernel-auto-reboot.sh reads `reboot`. A REBOOT is strictly larger than a deploy — it kills every container AND every host process — so a host that declares `reboot` must classify EVERY one of its rows for it; scripts/check-cron-interlock-coverage.mjs reports an unclassified row INDETERMINATE.

_reboot_rule: Under a REBOOT there is no post-kill catch-up launcher, so a `preempt-and-catchup` row IN FLIGHT => the harness DEFERS (next eligible run), unless the row records a measured `reboot_recovery`. A `no-safe-kill` row in flight => ABORTED, retried on the next run. `safe-to-kill` rows are never probed.
